verdict.rationale: Godot projects are stored as plain-text scenes/resources on local disk (godot-docs-9, godot-docs-17) and the engine itself is fully open-source under the permissive MIT license (godot-gh-2, godot-docs-16, godot-docs-23), meaning there is no vendor lock-in and a user can always take their project files and leave. However, there is no explicit 'data export' feature, no documented interchange/export format spec beyond the engine's own resource files, and no llms.txt/API for exporting engine-managed metadata (godot-probe-1, godot-probe-3). Missing for 10: explicit data-portability documentation, a defined open interchange format spec for projects, and evidence of exporting non-file engine state (e.g., editor settings, asset library metadata) in an open format.
